`<<` is not a Mentl token. SYNTAX's enumeration has no shift, `<` is TLt and
`|` is variant-separation, so `(arena << K) | offset` does not lex — and the
wheel it described contains zero `<<` in 60,500 lines, decoding the same
handle with `/` and `%` two functions away (spine_band, spine_slot). Two live
design sites said it: PLAN §11 Arc B′ and RESIDUE's judge-once entry.

The shape was wrong with the notation, which is the part worth catching. A
hand-packed bitfield is position-as-identity — drift 8 at the representation
layer — written into a surface whose own §5.U forbids the surface to carry a
representation decision. A handle is a two-field product {arena, offset};
one-word occupancy is a repr pin read at lower. memcpy-serializability holds
for the reason it always did, with no authored packing.

The class is banked rather than patched. doc-truth checks identity claims,
state claims are unchecked (its own peer), and NOTATION claims were not named
at all until a reader asked whether the operator existed. The close is the
docs' Mentl spans going through the medium's own lexer, not another grep row
in a script that mentl verify is condemned to replace.

The ev-seam: an effectful callee bound AFTER its caller generalized never
entered the caller's frozen row, so derive_ev_slots — which read
effects_of(lookup_ty(callee_handle)) — got [], lowered the call to a bare LCall,
and the callee's strict ev_perform_entry key-scan met an empty region and
faulted (m3 trapped in pre_register_fn_sig via each, the first infer perform).

escaping_row (the flow-closure: own_dispatched union callees' escaping minus
handled) was already built and precomputed at lower_program precisely to recover
those forward-ref-dropped effects — its own doc names derive_ev_slots as the
consumer — but derive_ev_slots was never wired to it. Wire it: evidence_effects_of
unions the per-call-site leaf (concrete, a higher-order arg's effect) with the
callee's flow-closure (forward-ref recovery). Keyed identity makes over-placement
tolerant, so the union is safe; each side alone drops a real case.

threads sst_ evidence and runs exit 9. m2 gate 8/0 rungs + 45/0 micros, no
regression. m3 assembles (0 errors) and now runs PAST the pre_register seam — the
trap marched to infer_fn's inf_exit_fn (a distinct frame-record-type flooring,
field-offset-unprovable). m3.wat 285k->513k lines: the correct forward-ref
evidence threading, previously dropped. The escaping_row esc_assoc O(n) lookup and
the deeper order-free-live-row form (leaf == flow-closure, union dissolves) are
named efficiency follow-ups.

perennials/10247f9:
The weekly refresh almost certainly never fired. setInterval(fn, DAY_MS) only
ticks after 24 hours of unbroken uptime, and every deploy or container recycle
resets it to zero. Boot only asked whether the table was empty, never whether the
data was stale, so a restart was a missed refresh rather than a catch-up. Check
staleness on boot and hourly instead; the check is one query, and the refresh
still only runs past the 7-day mark.

Enrichment never refreshed at all. Plants that Permapeople added after the sweeps
arrived with attracts NULL and bloom unchecked, and nothing ever filled them in,
so they could never surface in an "attracts bees" search. Run every sweep after a
source refresh; each one only touches rows it has not done, so this costs nothing
but the newcomers.

Companions could not refresh either. That sweep lived only in the retired
build-time pipeline, so the server preserved the 187 seeded links but had no way
to find new ones. Port it, with a one-time backfill that marks the
already-swept population instead of firing 8,600 redundant calls at a small
community server.
